messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up: Performance evaluation plan for KestrelAI

Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call so the team at Kestrel has clear expectations and we can align the benchmark work.

Recap (what we heard):
- Goal: determine production latency and throughput tradeoffs for your LLM workload across Redwood and your current hyperscaler endpoint.
- Success signal: p95 latency under ~200ms for typical 1k-token requests, p99 under ~450ms for the same profile, and sustained tokens/sec that keep cost within your budget envelope.
- Constraints: data residency in us-west, model weights are the cached open checkpoint you referenced, and request mix is 60% short (<64 tokens), 30% medium (64-512), 10% long (512-2000).

Proposed evaluation plan (high level):
1) A/B throughput pass: run side-by-side steady-state throughput tests at three QPS points (low/med/high) using your sample prompt deck — measure tokens/sec, mean/p95/p99 latency, and cost per 1M tokens.
2) p95/p99 focused bursts: small number of multi-second bursts to capture tail latency under load (cache warm vs cold).
3) Kernel/quantization parity: run on Redwood default quantized profile vs hyperscaler runtime (we'll note any precision differences).
4) Regression tests: run a small eval set to confirm generation parity (semantic checks) — not a full eval.

Deliverables & timing:
- Draft test matrix and scripts (we’ll share by EOD 6/30) — attached is a one-page summary of Redwood vs hyperscaler expectations.
- Run tests: target window 7/1–7/2 (we can slide if you need procurement signoff).
- Results & debrief: preliminary numbers within 48 hours of test completion; full write-up within 5 business days.

Ask from you before we start:
- Confirm the model variant and exact Docker/image you want us to spin up (you mentioned open-ckpt-v3-small?).
- Provide a read-only API key or test endpoint for the hyperscaler baseline and an ehr-ish sample of the prompt deck (or a Drive link).
- Confirm procurement contact if we need to exchange a short data-processing addendum.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-summary.pdf (one-pager), sample test matrix (inline).

Thanks — planning to loop in Rishi for the test-run details and Marissa for results communication.

— Sofia

- Procurement: procurement@kestrel.ai will need the eval scope and an LOE estimate for dedicated test time if you need private infra.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Looping in the SRE/bench team and dropping the explicit runbook we will follow. High-level notes: 

Planned infra & config:
- Redwood hosted nodes in us-west-2 using T4-equivalent for parity with Kestrel's baseline; runtime will use Redwood quantized FP8 profile unless Kestrel requests FP16 comparison.
- Continuous batching enabled with target latency SLO 200ms p95 for medium requests.

Test matrix (short):
- Phase A: Steady-state QPS at {5, 25, 100} with 15-minute windows. Capture tokens/sec, mean/p95/p99 per window, memory usage, and 95th request size.
- Phase B: Burst tests — 5x short bursts (30s) at QPS=200 to capture tail behavior and cold KV miss patterns.
- Phase C: Accuracy parity set — run 200 eval prompts and record top-1 token divergence metric and a handful of manual checks.

Measurement details:
- p95/p99 calculation: sliding windows of 1s, reported as aggregated percentiles over the run.
- Tokens/sec: server-side token accounting (not client-side) to avoid clock skew.

Requirements we need from Kestrel (please send ASAP):
- Read-only artifact URL or model checksum.
- Drive link with the 1000-prompt sample deck (Alex said he’ll send the token).
- Contact for procurement if we need an access window on their hyperscaler account.

Attachments: ma_plan_draft.docx (short mutual action plan; edit/comment welcome).

I’ll provision the test jobs tonight and post the test dashboard link in the drive. If procurement needs anything, Sofia, please coordinate.

— Rishi

Alex — we provisioned the runs and scheduled them for tomorrow (7/2) morning PT per your window. Summary of what we will run and asks in one place: 

What Redwood will run: 
- Steady-state tests at QPS: 5 / 25 / 100 (15m each) — measure tokens/sec, mean/p95/p99.
- 5x 30s bursts at QPS=200 to capture tails.
- Quantized FP8 profile + optional FP16 run if you confirm.
- Accuracy parity: 200 sample prompts.

Targets & reporting: 
- Immediate targets for this eval: p95 < 200ms median expectation; p99 under 450ms on warmed caches for the medium 64–512 token bucket. If we miss, we’ll capture KV patterns and batching artifacts and propose knob changes.
- Cost calc: we’ll report cost per 1M tokens for each run and an expected steady-state cost curve.

What we still need from you: 
- Read-only artifact URL or checksum (upload to the Drive share Alex will send).
- Hyperscaler test API token (short-lived) so we can reproduce your baseline.
- Procurement confirmation for data-processing addendum if needed.

I’ve attached the one-pager and the mutual action plan. If procurement is good with our short test window, we’ll proceed tomorrow morning and post live dashboards to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PerfDashboardMock

Please reply to confirm or flag any blockers. If you prefer a quick sync before we start, I’m free 7/2 8:30–9:15 PT.
